metadata.title: Automating the YouTube Review Pipeline
metadata.purpose: Pitch: what of the fellow-video review loop can be automated, and what cannot.
metadata.author: Vikhyat Raghumanda
metadata._channel_note: metadata.channel deliberately OMITTED. Setting it to claude-hai makes GATE L rule 7 enforce the fixed series kicker 'Irreducibly Human'. This is an outsider's pitch artifact, not an episode of their series, so it carries the HAI chip without claiming the series name.
metadata._voice_note: am_michael — Kokoro, free and local. Plain register, suggestive not assertive.
metadata._tone_note: REGISTER: confident, never blaming. State findings flatly - they are facts about code and about YouTube, not judgements about people. Do NOT hedge ('I may be wrong', 'correct me if', 'as far as I can tell') and do NOT assign fault ('nobody wrote the code', 'already shipped wrong', 'wasted').
metadata._ask_note: NO ASK. The reel does not request permission, interest, or information. It states the path and what each stage needs. Do not reintroduce questions to the viewer.
metadata._cut_note: B05 (HaiRenderDefaultDrift) CUT. Its claim - that failures come from fellows on an older copy - is disproven: brutalist.art's first commit (279e925, 22 Jul 2026) already sets HEIGHT=2160. Do not reinstate. The component and its render remain on disk, unused.

beats.new_visual_element: Claude composer: the ask lands answered, three ways
beats.narration_text: Here's a question worth asking about how fellow videos get reviewed. How much of it can be automated? The answer splits three ways. The sorting: most of it. The uploading: after two decisions that are yours to make. The judging: that stays with the professors.

props.command: How much of the video review loop can we automate?
output: UPLOADING   → after two decisions that are yours

show.event: composer opens, greeting reads 'Hi, Humanitarians AI'
command types in
send arms, running indicator appears
three output lines land in sequence

beats.new_visual_element: Hesitant writer: the framing typed, reconsidered, corrected
beats.narration_text: Every submission goes up to YouTube before anyone can tell whether it's usable. That's how the answer gets found today. But part of that answer is already sitting in the file, before the upload ever starts.

props.text: The review loop needs more hands.

show.event: types 'The review loop needs more hands.'
'hands' marks in terracotta — about to be reconsidered
deletes and retypes to 'checks'
settles on 'The review loop needs more checks.'

shot._prop_note: The reframe is the argument, and it blames nobody: not more effort, just an earlier check. Word-level swap is all this component does.

beats.new_visual_element: The manual loop as a five-stage rail; the delete branch stays lit
beats.narration_text: Here's the loop. A video arrives. It gets uploaded. You wait for processing. You check the resolution. Some get kept, some don't. All of that happens before you find out which.

show.event: five stages draw left to right
a file token travels the rail
the DELETE branch lights terracotta and stays lit
everything upstream dims to ~40% - the wasted span

shot._lead: HaiBrutalistE01Pipeline is the closest existing component (RENDERABLE, right register) but its stage labels are hardcoded and its only prop is sparkLine. Build a sibling in that file.

beats.new_visual_element: Two files, dimensions counting up against a 4K threshold line
beats.narration_text: YouTube isn't judging quality at this step. It's counting pixels. Above a certain size a 4K option appears, and below it, it doesn't. That same answer can be read straight from the file first, in about a second.

show.event: two file cards side by side, dimensions blank
readouts count up: left settles 3840x2160, right stops at 2560x1440
threshold line draws across both; left crosses, right does not
left stamps 4K, right stamps not-4K

beats.new_visual_element: A file that measures 4K, peeled back to a 720p piece being stretched
beats.narration_text: There's a wrinkle worth knowing about. Brutalist scales an undersized piece up to fill the frame, and on the video path there's no warning when it does. So a file can measure a full 4K and still look soft, because one piece underneath it was smaller.

show.event: probe readout returns 3840x2160 with a green tick
frame peels back: one piece underneath reads 1280x720
that piece stretches to fill the frame, edges visibly softening
stamp lands: 'no warning issued'

beats.new_visual_element: Stage one: folder watch, two-way sort, note written, nothing deleted
beats.narration_text: So the first piece is a small one. A script watches the folder and checks each new file against the target before anything goes up. Passes one way, the rest the other, with a note saying what to fix. Nothing gets deleted. And the check isn't new. There's already a place for it in the toolkit's own notes.

props.title: Check before uploading
props.note: re-pull the toolkit, then render again
props.sparkLine: there is already a place for it

show.event: stage chip: STAGE 1 - check before uploading
folder watcher pulses; a file lands
the file routes down one of two paths
a note card writes itself into the fail path
counter under the fail folder holds at deleted: 0

beats.new_visual_element: An HAI video carrying the wrong channel's handle, flagged
beats.narration_text: There's a second thing worth checking in the same pass. A Humanitarians AI video should close with the Humanitarians AI outro. Whether it does can be read straight from the files, without anyone watching a frame. It costs almost nothing to add.

props.precedent: easy to miss, easy to check

show.event: settings file opens, channel reads @HumanitariansAI
the outro resolves to the wrong component, handle reads @NikBearBrown
mismatch flag fires between the two
cut to the documented precedent line

beats.new_visual_element: Stage two sorts the folder; stage three moves the check upstream
beats.narration_text: From there it goes two ways. Point the same check at the folder, and the sorting stops being manual. Or move it earlier, so it flags before a render finishes and fellows update first. The second is the better fix, and the bigger change.

props.sparkLine: catch it later, or avoid it earlier

show.event: stage 2 chip; the sort runs on the folder, hands-off
the frame slides left; stage 3 chip enters
the check jumps upstream, into the tool itself
a failing render is refused before it ever finishes

beats.new_visual_element: Stage four and the two steps only the organisation can take
beats.narration_text: The last piece, uploading, needs two things that are yours to decide. Videos uploaded through an unapproved Google project stay private, so the first question is whether there's already an approved one. And the authorising has to come from whoever owns the channel. It can't be handed over. I'd show you the steps.

props.notMine: I'd show the steps. The key stays with you.

show.event: stage chip: STAGE 4
card one lands and stamps LOCKED, held longest
card two: an owner-only authorisation, delegation crossed out
closing line: I show the procedure, I never hold the key

shot._fact_note: VERIFIED. Private lock: projects created after 28 July 2020. Delegation impossible: invited channel managers cannot manage via YouTube APIs, and service accounts return NoLinkedYouTubeAccount. The daily-upload-cap claim was CUT - uploads now sit in their own allowance at 100/day, so it is not a constraint. See FACTCHECK.md.

beats.new_visual_element: Your turn: the prompt, and the three questions
beats.narration_text: Your turn. Here's a prompt you can point at the repository to see what actually sets the render height. And here's the whole path. Stage one needs nothing from anyone. Stage two needs the folder. Stage four needs the two decisions on the last slide. That's the route, start to finish.

props.command: Read the Brutalist repo and tell me what actually sets the render height.
output: STAGE 3  → a change to the toolkit
